summary: A seat's host pushes the other members, over a new member-authenticated peer route, when it last heard each of its seats, so another member's card and mail holds hear a resting seat whose unchanged re-stamps stay in its host's local log

replay.detail: No claim is written or read differently; pushed times are kept in memory only.

schema.detail: daemon.started's features object gains seat_freshness = 1, an additive optional key. No table or claim field changes.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Contract C3 of the claims-store breakup (approved). New peer route POST /v1/peer/seat-freshness, member-authenticated and signed like the other peer routes, recorded through the daemon's /v1/internal/seat-freshness. The push is reactive: a commit wakes the host's pusher, which within 10 seconds reads its seats' newest local harness.observed in one statement and sends each other member, or configured peer, whose own newest daemon.started advertises seat_freshness = 1 only the seats that changed since its last push there, every member at once; a member whose daemon.started changed gets every seat, and a failed push is retried a minute later. The receiver records only seats its declarations place on the sender, keeping the newest time, and answers with the seats it recorded; a seat it left out (its declaration has not arrived yet) stays owed, and the host retries it a minute later without waiting for a commit, then less often, up to every 15 minutes, while it stays owed. An agent card's observation, its stale-idle lapse and the down rule, and the mail hold's freshness, read the latest of the replicated report, the local log and that time. An older member is never pushed to and keeps its replicated re-stamps; a worker without the route records nothing. No client field or value changes.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

manual.detail: No manual step. A member that is not in a fleet pushes to nobody.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting stops the pushing and the receiving; a reverted member's next daemon.started no longer advertises the route, so its peers stop pushing to it.
